This week, I’m sharing a peek into an exciting conversation I had with Dr. Myechia Minter-Jordan, CEO of AARP. Minter-Jordan is the first person featured in my new series, The Career Switch, which highlights real people who have made successful career pivots in the face of a changing economy.  Minter-Jordan started her career treating patients as an internal medicine physician, but her interest in the systems shaping patient care eventually led her from medicine to management—and ultimately to the top job at AARP. Now in her 50s, Minter-Jordan says her nonlinear career is proof that making a major pivot doesn’t mean starting over. The key, she says, is recognizing the transferable skills you already have and being open to where they might take you next. See below for some of my top takeaways from that interview: Were there any specific lessons you had to learn or unlearn as you made the transition from physician to executive? I had to learn how decisions were made. Often they’re not made or influenced by the loudest person in the room. They’re influenced by the person who has the credibility, who comes prepared to those meetings, who speaks with authority, but who also is listening. There are lots of nuances to being a leader that we don’t learn in a classroom and that we learn by being in these spaces where there are people of power making really impactful decisions. I learned those softer skills in those spaces.  As someone who transitioned from working in a hospital, to being a corporate executive at a healthcare company, to now leading a nonprofit, what advice do you have for people trying to decide if now is the right time to make a career pivot? Things aren’t always linear. Some opportunities come to you and you have to not just think about the specific role, but the skills that allowed you to be successful in your current role and how those might be transferable to the next role. An example of that that I’ll give is as a physician, I’ve been trained to triage. So when I encounter a situation, I’m immediately thinking about what are the things that are most urgent versus less urgent, and then that helps shape my decision making. So I’ve taken those skills and used them in what I do today.  Also, let your values guide who you are as an individual. My values are transparency, respect, accountability and communication. 78407.subject: AVALANCHE AUGUST 2026 RECAP
78407.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.team1.blog/p/avalanche-august-2026-recap

August was the month Wall Street started showing up on Avalanche in earnest. Charles Schwab added AVAX for its 40 million brokerage accounts, Dinari brought 724 tokenized U.S. stocks including the full S&P 500 to Avalanche investors, and POSCO International completed a proof of concept for tokenizing global trade receivables on the network.
At the same time, Team1 officially launched in Korea. With Avalanche Summit NYC less than three weeks away, September is shaping up to be a major moment for the ecosystem.
Here’s everything that happened in August.
Want to keep up with the latest in the Avalanche ecosystem? Subscribe to the Team1 blog and get our updates in your inbox weekly.
Tokenized Assets Grow Nearly 8x in a Year:
Tokenized assets on Avalanche climbed from $242 million to $1.93 billion over the past year, with Securitize now accounting for more than half of that value. [Growth [ https://substack.com/redirect/5fc6043c-d884-4242-90b9-611b3d9b8308?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ]]
Foundation Introduces Gross Chain Income:
The Avalanche Foundation published a new Gross Chain Income framework from Lead Economist Eric Lu, extending its Gross Chain Product work into a three-step model for measuring, capturing, and distributing value across the ecosystem. [GCI [ https://substack.com/redirect/92d16235-ee07-40f6-a010-1a719e9a302b?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ]]
RWA Transfer Volume Jumps 360% in 30 Days:
Avalanche’s RWA ecosystem recorded $365.29 million in 30-day transfer volume, up 360.15% from the prior month, spanning tokenized funds, equities, treasuries, and private credit. [Volume [ https://substack.com/redirect/183ebb6c-4c8e-4af8-ad57-0c24db4d6fce?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ]]
Team1 Korea Officially Launches:
Team1 Korea launched after onboarding more than 500 builders, 12 teams, 200-plus developers, and 80-plus founders, giving Korean talent a clearer path to build on Avalanche.
Team1 Chapters Stay Busy Across Five Continents:
Team1 chapters continued bringing Avalanche directly to local builders. August highlights included a builder workshop in Seoul focused on AI-agent payments, a meetup in Reggio Calabria, a Builder Connect at Oracle’s Bogotá offices, an L1 workshop in Türkiye, university activity in Vietnam, and multiple builder and community events across Brazil, India, Latin America, Nigeria and lots more.
New paths for funding and support opened up this month.
Team1 Opens Applications for ProtocolCamp Cohort 10:
Team1 called for builders to join ProtocolCamp Cohort 10, a 12-week program turning ideas into shipped products with travel covered and a kickoff during Korea Blockchain Week. [ProtocolCamp [ https://substack.com/redirect/484aea27-85f1-40c0-922a-43f8706045a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEW

78395.subject: Micro-burnout – tichý zabijak produktivity, o ktorom sa stále hovorí príliš málo
78395.body:
Správy, na ktorých záleží

Автор: Startitup


Автор: Startitup

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/micro-burnout-tich%C3%BD-zabijak-produktivity-o-ktorom-sa-st%C3%A1le-hovor%C3%AD-joqsf?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3Bq2NgTYyaR0uz7c9x3wiP3A%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=2bB-QzMogxPco1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mtjt4xb4~ul-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mtjt4xb4-ul
  
Únava, ktorá nikdy úplne neprejde. Pocit, že pracujeme celý deň, no večer máme dojem, akoby sme neurobili nič podstatné. Strácame motiváciu, horšie sa sústredíme a aj jednoduché úlohy nám zaberajú viac času ako kedysi. Väčšina ľudí by nepovedala, že ide o vyhorenie. Veď stále chodia do práce, plnia si svoje povinnosti a navonok fungujú rovnako ako predtým. Práve preto je micro-burnout taký nebezpečný. Nejde pritom len o subjektívny pocit. Výskumy v oblasti pracovnej psychológie dlhodobo ukazujú, že časté prerušovanie práce a neustále prepínanie medzi úlohami znižujú schopnosť sústredenia aj kvalitu výkonu. Profesorka Sophie Leroy vo svojej dnes už často citovanej štúdii opísala fenomén attention residue – stav, keď časť našej pozornosti zostáva pri predchádzajúcej úlohe aj po tom, čo sme sa už presunuli na ďalšiu. Výsledkom je pomalšie rozhodovanie, viac chýb a nižšia efektivita práce.  Nie každé vyhorenie prichádza naraz Keď sa povie syndróm vyhorenia, väčšina z nás si predstaví človeka, ktorý je na pokraji síl, dlhodobo nezvláda pracovné tempo a nakoniec musí na niekoľko týždňov alebo mesiacov úplne vypnúť. Realita je však často oveľa nenápadnejšia. Existujú obdobia, keď človek ešte nie je vyhorený v klinickom zmysle slova, no dlhodobo funguje pod tlakom, ktorý sa postupne podpisuje na jeho energii, motivácii aj výkone. Práve tento stav sa čoraz častejšie označuje ako micro-burnout. Nevzniká z jednej veľkej krízy. Vzniká z desiatok malých každodenných situácií – neustáleho prepínania medzi úlohami, nekonečných porád, notifikácií, telefonátov, e-mailov, tlaku na okamžitú reakciu či pocitu, že človek musí byť dostupný prakticky nepretržite. Každý z týchto faktorov sa môže zdať zanedbateľný. Spolu však vytvárajú prostredie, v ktorom mozog takmer nikdy nedostane priestor na skutočné sústredenie ani oddych. Produktivitu neznižuje len množstvo práce Firmy prirodzene hľadajú spôsoby, ako zvýšiť efektivitu. Zavádzajú nové technológie, automatizujú procesy a nastavujú výkonové ukazovatele. Popritom však často prehliadajú jeden dôležitý fakt. Najväčším nepriateľom produktivity nemusí byť objem práce, ale spôsob, akým počas dňa pracujeme. Ak zamestnanec každých pár minút prepína medzi e-mailami, chatmi, telefonátmi a stretnutiami, jeho mozog spotrebúva značnú časť energie len na opätovné sústredenie. Nejde pritom o ojed
